verdict.rationale: Context.dev documents its own job-visibility features: async batch crawls you can track to completion, partial-result completion markers, and per-interaction success checks. These cover a thin slice of job monitoring and output validation. Its signed change events are for website content changes, not job-failure alerts, so they don't count toward alerting. Missing for 10: job performance metrics or dashboards, explicit data-quality validation rules, failure alerts or notifications for failed jobs, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can monitor job performance, validate data quality, and receive alerts when something fails

citations.quote: Crawl up to 25,000 pages in a background batch, track progress, and retrieve Markdown or HTML when the job finishes.
Return usable completed work with a completion marker. If no usable result exists, fail without a charge.
Click, wait, or scroll before scraping or extracting a page, then check which interactions succeeded.
